passages.title: Rainforests of the Sea
passages.passage: Few ecosystems on Earth are (1)____ once so productive and so fragile as a coral reef. Although reefs cover less than one per cent of the ocean floor, they are home (2)____ roughly a quarter of all marine species, a density of life that has earned them the nickname 'rainforests of the sea'. The reef itself is built by tiny animals called polyps, which secrete a limestone skeleton and live in partnership with microscopic algae. It is these algae, rather (3)____ the polyps themselves, that give a healthy reef its colour. When the surrounding water grows too warm, the polyps expel their algae and the reef turns a ghostly white, a process (4)____ as bleaching. Not (5)____ the temperature drops again can the partnership be restored, and if the heat persists for more than a few weeks the polyps simply starve. Scientists had long assumed that bleaching was a rare event; (6)____ the past two decades, however, it has struck the world's largest reefs repeatedly. Had governments acted on the earliest warnings, some of that damage (7)____ have been avoided. Even so, not all the news is bleak. Certain reefs in the Red Sea appear to tolerate heat far (8)____ than their Pacific cousins, and researchers are now trying to work (9)____ whether the genes responsible could be encouraged elsewhere. Whether such efforts succeed will depend largely (10)____ how quickly the oceans keep warming.

questions.explanation: At once ... and ... means 'simultaneously both': at once so productive and so fragile. All or for cannot combine with once to carry that meaning.
A place is home to the species that live there. Of and for do not follow home in this sense.
Rather than contrasts the algae with the polyps inside a cleft sentence. Then is a time adverb and not would need and not.
A reduced relative clause: a process (which is) known as bleaching; described as also works. Called and named fail because they take a bare noun, never as.

Not until (or till, before) at the front of a sentence triggers the inversion can the partnership be restored. When would give the reverse meaning: that recovery never happens at the moment the water cools.

A period measured up to now takes over, in, during, throughout or within with the present perfect has struck. Since fails because it needs a starting point, not a length of time; for fails before the past two decades with this verb pattern in formal prose.
An inverted third conditional (Had governments acted ...) needs a past modal: might, could or would have been avoided. Should fails because it turns a hypothetical result into advice about the past.
Tolerate heat far better than compares how well they cope; more is also acceptable. Best is a superlative and cannot precede than; well is not comparative.
The phrasal verb work out means discover by reasoning. Work on means continue improving something, and work at means make an effort, so neither can take a whether clause.
Depend on (or upon) is the only preposition the verb takes, even with an adverb like largely in between. Of and from are common learner errors influenced by independent of.

passages.title: Letters Made of Lead
passages.passage: It is hard to overstate how thoroughly the printing press transformed the way (1)____ which knowledge moved around Europe in the fifteenth century. Before movable type, a single manuscript might take a monk the better (2)____ of a year to copy, and every copy carried the errors of the one before it. No sooner (3)____ Johannes Gutenberg's workshop begun producing Bibles than printers in other cities started to imitate his methods, and within fifty years presses were operating in more than two hundred towns. What made the invention so powerful was not the press (4)____ but the combination of cheap paper, oil-based ink and metal letters that could be rearranged endlessly. Scholars who had once relied (5)____ memory could now compare identical texts hundreds of miles apart, which in (6)____ made it possible to spot mistakes and build on one another's work. Not everyone welcomed the change. Some rulers, fearing the spread of ideas they could not control, (7)____ about licensing every printer in their territory; others simply banned books outright. Yet (8)____ hard they tried, the flow of pamphlets proved impossible to stop. Had the press never been invented, the religious and scientific upheavals of the following century would almost certainly have (9)____ a very different course. Historians still argue over how much credit one man deserves, but few would deny that the world he left behind bore little (10)____ to the one he had been born into.

questions.explanation: The formal relative structure is the way in which something happens. By or on do not collocate with way here; that would need to replace which, not sit beside it.
The better part of a period means most of it. Half gives the wrong quantity and does not take better; portion is not the idiom.

No sooner had + subject + past participle ... than is a fixed inversion with the past perfect. Did fails because the participle begun follows, and was would need begun to be passive, which makes no sense.

Not the press itself but the combination uses the emphatic reflexive to isolate the machine from its context; alone works the same way. Only fails because it must precede the noun, and self is not a free-standing word.
You rely on or upon something. In and to are common errors modelled on trust in and refer to, but rely never takes them.
In turn means 'as a further consequence' and links one result to the next. Return gives in return, an exchange, which is not the meaning; fact would merely add emphasis.

Set about (or went about) doing something means started to tackle it; thought about licensing (merely considered it) is also grammatical and fits the contrast with rulers who simply banned books. Started or began fail because they take to or a bare gerund, never about.
However hard they tried means 'no matter how hard'. Whatever must be followed by a noun, and although cannot precede a bare adverb like hard.
Events take (or follow, run, pursue) a course; the past participle is needed after would have. Had or gone do not form this collocation, and the base form take cannot follow have.

Bear little resemblance to is the standard collocation; bore little relation to and bore little similarity to are also accepted. Difference reverses the logic, and likeness is not used with bear ... to in this way.

passages.title: What the Brain Does at Night
passages.passage: For most of the twentieth century, sleep was regarded as little (1)____ than a period of rest, a nightly shutdown during which the brain did nothing of importance. That view has been overturned so completely that many neuroscientists now describe sleep as the point (2)____ which learning actually happens. During the day, new experiences are stored temporarily in a region called the hippocampus, but the record is fragile and easily overwritten. It is only at night, (3)____ the brain is cut off from fresh input, that these traces are replayed and gradually transferred to the cortex for long-term storage. Researchers have demonstrated this in a series of elegant experiments. Volunteers who learned a list of word pairs in the evening and then slept remembered far more the next morning than those who had stayed awake, (4)____ though both groups had been given the same amount of time. Nor does the benefit stop at facts. Musicians who practise a difficult passage and then sleep on it often play it more fluently the following day, (5)____ having touched the instrument in between. What is less clear is (6)____ the different stages of sleep contribute. Deep, slow-wave sleep appears to strengthen factual memories, (7)____ the dreaming stage seems to link new information to what we already know. There is a warning here for students. Staying up all night before an exam may feel productive, but (8)____ it is followed by sleep, much of the effort is wasted. Far from being time lost, then, sleep turns (9)____ to be the very process by (10)____ knowledge is made permanent.

questions.explanation: Little more than means 'hardly anything beyond'. Less reverses the sense, and other would need little other than, which is not idiomatic English.
The point at which is the formal equivalent of the point when. In and on do not collocate with point in a time sense, and of would make the sentence meaningless.

A time conjunction introduces the clause: when, once, while, after or as the brain is cut off. Which fails because the clause already has its own subject, and that would wrongly close the cleft sentence early.
Even though concedes the fact that both groups had equal time. As would produce as though, which means 'as if' and turns the fact into an appearance.

Without having touched uses the preposition plus perfect gerund to say the practice did not happen. Despite is impossible because the meaning is not concessive, and not would need not having touched in a different position.
A noun clause is needed after is: how, what or whether the stages contribute. That fails because the sentence says the matter is unclear, so a fact cannot simply be stated.
Two stages are contrasted, so while or whereas (or simply and / but) joins the clauses. Although fails because the two facts are not in tension, and however cannot join clauses with just a comma.
Unless it is followed by sleep means 'if it is not'. If says the opposite, that sleep causes the waste, and until would make the wasted effort a temporary state.
Turn out to be means prove to be, after investigation. Turn up means appear, and turn in means go to bed, so neither takes to be.
After a preposition the relative pronoun must be which: the process by which. That can never follow a preposition, and what would leave process without a relative clause.

passages.title: Born of Fire, Claimed by the Sea
passages.passage: Volcanic islands are among the youngest pieces of land on the planet, and their life story follows a pattern that geologists can now (1)____ with remarkable precision. Most begin far below the surface, where a plume of molten rock forces its way (2)____ the ocean crust. Eruption after eruption piles lava on the sea floor until, often after hundreds of thousands of years, a cone finally breaks the surface. At this stage the new island is little more (3)____ bare black rock, utterly hostile to life. Yet colonisation begins almost immediately. Seeds arrive on the wind or in the stomachs of birds; insects are blown in on storms; lichens take (4)____ on the cooling lava and slowly grind it into soil. Within a few centuries, what was once a sterile heap of cinders may support a forest. The island's (5)____, however, is already sealed. As the tectonic plate carries it away from the plume that created it, the volcano falls silent and erosion sets (6)____. Waves eat at the coastline, rain carves valleys, and the whole mass gradually sinks under its own weight. In warm seas, coral reefs grow up around the shrinking peak, so that (7)____ the island has disappeared entirely, a ring of reef remains to mark where it stood. The Hawaiian chain illustrates this cycle perfectly: the youngest island, still erupting, sits at one end, (8)____ a line of ever older, ever lower islands stretches away to the north-west. Thanks (9)____ this sequence, scientists can estimate how fast the plate is moving. Few natural laboratories offer (10)____ a clear picture of creation and decay unfolding side by side.

questions.q: Blank (1): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: Scientists reconstruct a sequence of past events from evidence. Rebuild and restore apply to physical objects, and recover means get back something lost.

questions.q: Blank (2): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: Magma forces its way through a layer, passing from one side to the other. Across, over and along describe movement on a surface, not penetration.

questions.q: Blank (3): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: Little more than is a comparative and needs than. As pairs with as much, then is a time adverb, and that would need a full clause to follow.

questions.q: Blank (4): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: Take hold means become established. Take place means happen, take shape means develop a form, and take grip is not an English expression.

questions.q: Blank (5): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: Only a fate can be sealed, meaning fixed beyond change. Luck, fortune and chance refer to random outcomes and do not take this verb.

questions.q: Blank (6): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: An unwelcome process such as erosion, rot or bad weather sets in, meaning begins and continues. Set up means establish, set off means depart or trigger, and set out means begin a journey or explain.

questions.q: Blank (7): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: Once the island has disappeared means 'after that point', which is when the ring of reef is all that remains. While would place the two events at the same time, and unless and until would say the reef survives only if the island does not vanish.

questions.q: Blank (8): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: While here contrasts the two ends of the chain, like whereas. Although signals an unexpected exception, and unless and until express condition and time, neither of which fits a description.

questions.q: Blank (9): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: Thanks to is a fixed prepositional phrase meaning 'because of'. Thanks for expresses gratitude and needs a person, and by and of never follow thanks.

questions.q: Blank (10): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: Such a clear picture is the order before an article plus adjective plus noun. So and too would need so clear a picture, and very cannot precede the article at all.
